title: Comfort Veg Bibimbap (Black Rice + Gochujang Bowl)
style: Nutty black rice bowl loaded with fresh crunchy veg, deep-golden crispy tofu, quick-pickled onions, and a thick gochujang drizzle — pure cozy comfort
description: A cozy, wholesome riff on bibimbap built on nutty black rice with deep-golden crispy tofu, rainbow veg arranged just-so, quick-pickled red onions, and a pourable gochujang sauce you'll want to put on everything. Warm rice meets cool crunch meets spicy-sweet heat — this is the bowl you make when you need a hug from dinner.

steps: Pickle the Onions First: Toss sliced red onion with vinegar, salt, and a pinch of sugar. Set aside — they'll be perfectly tangy and pink by the time you need them (minimum 10 minutes).

Cook the Black Rice: Rinse rice, combine with water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer and cover. Cook 30–35 minutes until tender with a slight chew. Don't overcook — the texture is everything in this bowl.
Prep the Tofu: While rice cooks, press tofu firmly between paper towels. Cube it, then toss with cornflour, salt, and garlic powder until every piece is coated.

Fry Until Properly Golden: Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high. Pan-fry tofu 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden with genuinely crispy edges. If it's still pale, keep going — pale tofu is sad tofu. Set aside.
Blanch the Spinach: Drop spinach into boiling water for 30–60 seconds. Drain immediately, squeeze out all the water (really wring it), then toss with a drizzle of sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Prep Remaining Veg: Cut carrots and cucumber into thin matchsticks. Slice bell pepper into thin strips. These stay raw — the fresh crunch is the counterpoint to the warm rice and crispy tofu.

Make the Gochujang Sauce: Whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, maple syrup, and water. It should be thick but pourable — add water a splash at a time. Taste it. If it needs more heat, add more gochujang. If it needs more sweet, another drop of maple.
Sauté the Power-Ups (Optional): If using mushrooms, sauté in a hot pan with a little oil until golden and slightly crispy at the edges. Set aside with the tofu.

Assemble with Intent: Divide warm black rice between bowls. Arrange each vegetable in its own section around the bowl — spinach, carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, pickled onions. Pile crispy tofu (and mushrooms if using) in the centre. Spoon a generous amount of gochujang sauce right in the middle. Add kimchi on the side if using.

Finish and Devour: Scatter toasted sesame seeds over everything. Drizzle with a final thread of sesame oil. Admire it for exactly two seconds — then mix everything together thoroughly right before eating. That's where the magic happens.
tips: The whole point is contrast: hot rice + hot tofu against cool, crunchy raw veg. Don't cook the carrots, cucumber, or pepper.
If your tofu isn't deeply golden and crispy, you pulled it too early. Give it time — this is what makes the bowl.
Black rice takes longer than white rice (30–35 min). Start it first and build everything around it.
The sauce keeps in the fridge for a week. Make double — you'll put it on rice, noodles, eggs, toast, your hand.
For maximum comfort mode: add sautéed mushrooms AND kimchi AND a fried egg. No rules, only vibes.
Leftovers reheat well — keep sauce and raw veg separate, then reassemble when ready to eat.
